production.note: US model years, from a database (last resort; no manufacturer or magazine page stating the US model years was found). First: KBB lists the 2015 Huracán with the single trim 'LP 610-4 Coupe 2D' and says 'The 2015 Lamborghini Huracan is all-new'; KBB has no 2014 Huracán page (404). Last: KBB's 2019 Huracán lists an 'AWD Coupe 2D' rated '602 @ 8250 RPM' (kbb-huracan-2019, kbb-huracan-2019-specs), i.e. the LP 610-4, and Guide Auto reports the Huracán EVO, 'the new generation of the Huracán', as the 2020 model (guideauto-huracan-evo-2020). Lamborghini release: show premiere at Geneva 2014, 'customer delivery scheduled to start in spring 2014'. The Spyder is a separate record.

body.note: Two-door coupe; the open car is sold as the Huracán LP 610-4 Spyder (separate record).

displacementL.note: 5,204 cc ('The displacement of 5,204 cm³ is the result of an 84.5 millimeter bore and 92.8 millimeter stroke.')

aspiration.note: Naturally aspirated V10 per the release

drivetrain.note: 'Four wheel drive with new hydraulic multi-plate clutch'

transmission.note: '7-speed dual-clutch transmission', Lamborghini Doppia Frizione (LDF); no manual offered

powerHp.note: Quote: "It produces a power output of 448 kW / 610 hp at 8,250 rpm and a maximum torque of 560 Nm at 6,500 rpm." The 610 is Lamborghini's metric (CV/PS) figure: 610 x 0.98632 = 602 hp. No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS. KBB is not consistent: its 2019 listing shows 602 hp, its 2015 listing 610. The release itself gives both 448 kW and 449 kW in different places; the 610 figure is the same in both. KBB prints Lamborghini's metric figure as hp; no hp rating from Lamborghini's US arm was found, so the guide's conversion is used.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (no curb weight for the standard car, and no optioned-car curb weight, was found from Lamborghini or a major magazine). Quote: "The ultralight chassis forms the basis for the vehicle's low dry weight of 1,422 kilograms; with its excellent stiffness, it guarantees the handling precision of a racing car." 1,422 x 2.20462 = 3,135 lb. Evo says this is for an optioned car (evo-huracan-used): "The launch car tipped the scales at 1422kg, but that's a dry weight figure with the lightest possible options." A standard car is heavier. Top Gear's auto-filled spec page prints 'Minimum Kerbweight 1,422kg' (topgear-huracan-spec), the same dry figure relabelled; not used as a curb weight.
